bullets.title: AI capex rebound confirmed: META/AVGO/GOOGL/ORCL mega-deals signal hyper-cycle continuation
bullets.body: META raising $97.5B (incl. $60B ATM), AVGO closing $63B SPV for custom chips, and SPCX executing $40B GPU deal signal sustained AI infrastructure buildout. GOOGL CFO flagged capex will increase significantly in 2027; ORCL diversifying chip supply to include GOOGL TPUs, CBRS wafer-scale, and SambaNova alongside Nvidia Vera Rubin. MegaCap earnings (AMZN, GOOGL, MSFT, INTC) this week are the critical near-term catalyst for the AI trade.

bullets.title: VRT surges 17%, GEV beats/raises — AI power infrastructure demand is accelerating, not plateauing
bullets.body: Vertiv posted 3Q revenues 15% above consensus with +55% organic growth and guided 4Q at +50% organic; stock +16.9% pre-market. GEV beat with $29B orders (+96% organically), raised FY26 FCF guidance 37.5% at mid-range to $16B-$17B, doubled buyback to $20B, and acquired Trench Group for $9B (13x '28 EBITDA). Combined results powerfully validate the AI power infrastructure demand narrative.

bullets.title: ENPH -20% pre-market: Q4 guide -32% below consensus; US solar recovery not in sight
bullets.body: Enphase Q4 revenue guided $225M-$255M vs FactSet $297.6M with gross margins 40%-43% vs consensus 44%; management signaled no meaningful US residential demand recovery. European sell-through fell 12% in 3Q; price cuts on energy storage are compressing margins. SEDG -10%, RUN -5% in sympathy; stock downgraded at both Oppenheimer and Roth Capital (PT cut to $30 from $55).

bullets.title: Tape: S&P +0.2% to 7,734, 10yr at 5.00%, WTI +2.1% to $102 — risk assets grinding higher with hawkish undertow
bullets.body: S&P 500 futures +0.19% to 7,772; VIX at 17.19 (+1.9%). The 10-year yield sits at exactly 5.00% with the 2-year at 4.75%, keeping the rates backdrop hawkish. WTI crude +$2.12 to $102, supporting energy/reflation names. Only 22% of stocks are beating implied earnings moves this cycle per Citi — realized vol remains muted despite the options market pricing larger swings.

bullets.title: Hedgeye macro: short semis/META/HYG, long oil; warns AI-bubble momentum trade is fragile
bullets.body: McCullough shorted HYG and Goldman Sachs, viewing the semi/credit rally as a speculative AI-bubble trade. He cited a $5.5B market-on-close buy imbalance in SOXL as evidence of retail chasing. KOSPI is down ~34% from cycle peak despite a 6% bounce; he plans to short SK Hynix and Korean semis. Macro posture: long Brent (targeting $122-$123), short Russell 2000 (~8% from peak), buying healthcare/staples defensively. UST 2yr hawkish, Bitcoin exposure fully exited.

bullets.title: Hedgeye October inflation nowcast raised to +3.84% y/y (+10bp); CPI release November 10
bullets.body: Hedgeye's monthly inflation model, which claims 90% directional accuracy on the CPI second derivative, has firmed during October, now pointing to +3.84% y/y — up 10bp from the start of the month. This reinforces the higher-for-longer rates narrative ahead of the November 10 CPI print and the upcoming FOMC meeting.

bullets.title: 3Q GDP tracking 3.2% but trade is a -3.0% to -3.5% drag, led by AI-related imports
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's September advance trade data show the goods deficit widened $2.8B to $134.9B (largest since Jan 2022 outside 1Q25), with real imports +1.3% m/m on capital goods and consumer goods demand. A separate PSC macro note flags a -3.0% to -3.5% trade drag on 3Q GDP — larger than Atlanta Fed's -2.9% estimate — driven primarily by surging AI-related import volumes and prices. Real GDP tracking unchanged at 3.2% q/q SAAR.

bullets.title: FOMC and Fed Chair Warsh: near-term press conference impact likely limited; breadth of committee views matters more
bullets.body: 22V notes that with Warsh speaking primarily for himself rather than the committee, the shelf life of any press conference impact is shorter than under prior Fed chairs. 62% of investors surveyed expect a mixed/negligible market reaction to the FOMC. The 2-year yield at 4.75% is already pricing a hawkish tilt; the broader committee tone over coming days will be more durable for risk assets.

bullets.title: STX beats/raises on HDD cycle strength; HAMR to represent ~70% of shipments in CY27
bullets.body: Seagate delivered a clean beat with GIR '28 EPS estimates up ~15% to ~$68.60; nearline shipments hit a record 198EB in the quarter. HAMR (Mozaic 4) technology expected to reach ~70% of shipments in CY27 with hyperscaler qualifications advancing. STX plans to significantly increase buybacks starting CY27. Note: Dec quarter EPS guide of ~$9.20 came in below the $9.50-$10 bogey due to product mix-shift, not execution — Summit Insights downgraded to Hold on moderating outperformance concerns.

bullets.title: ETSY +6.5%: active buyers grew y/y for first time in 2 years; FY26 GMS raised to ~7%
bullets.body: Etsy Q3 revenue $692.5M beat FactSet $668.1M; GMS +8.8% y/y with EBITDA margin expanding to 30.4%. The company raised FY26 GMS growth guidance to ~7% and maintained 4Q EBITDA margin ~30%. Internal personalization improvements via AI/ML contributed ~2 percentage points to annualized GMS growth in Q3. CFO Lanny Baker departing early March adds a transition risk overhang.

bullets.title: Visa F4Q26 beat; FY27 low-double-digit revenue/EPS guide meets elevated expectations, ~25% of volume up for renewal
bullets.body: Visa Q4 EPS $3.48 beat consensus $3.44 on payment volume +9.3% and cross-border +14% y/y; VAS grew 31%. FY27 guidance: net revenue low-double-digit, EPS low-double to low-teens, with ~25% of payment volume up for renewal vs. 20% in FY26 — elevated client incentives are the key risk. Agentic commerce estimated to add ~1-2% to top line by 2030. Sell-side avg PT moved to $443 (+3.1%).

bullets.title: Anthropic S-1 reveals compute costs scaling to $100B in 2027; FCF turns negative, valuation risk to lower end of $1.5-2tn range
bullets.body: 22V highlights that Anthropic's compute costs are ramping from ~$35B (2026) to ~$100B (2027) and ~$140B (2028), driving FCF negative in 2027-2028. Customers with $100K+ ARR more than doubled in Q3 alone to 11,900+; 48% of revenue flows through CSP channels. $390B in future commitments with CSPs ($270B non-cancelable) anchors the model but the lower end of the $1.5-2tn IPO range is seen as more likely to resonate with investors.

bullets.title: Hedgeye SHORT APP, LONG U: Vector passing $1B run rate early as budget shifts from AppLovin
bullets.body: APP missed its 2Q26 revenue guide midpoint for the first time in 15 quarters; Street cut FY28 EBITDA by 12%. Net revenue per install growth decelerated to 58% from 93%, and 3Q26 sequential growth guided at 7.6% vs. 17.5% in 3Q24. Unity's Vector grew 23% sequentially vs. internal plan of 12-13%; advertiser count up 37% since early July vs. 10% for APP, with 3 of 4 Unity buyers reporting better returns. U's commerce product projects $1.6B routed spending by 2028.

bullets.title: Midterm elections: TMT sector watching AI regulation, data center policy, and political ad spend outcomes
bullets.body: Multiple sell-side and macro shops (Hedgeye, Morgan Stanley, 22V) are flagging 2026 midterms as a key policy catalyst for AI regulation, data center buildout trajectory, and political advertising spend. Congressional control outcome will determine the regulatory posture on AI and the fiscal backdrop for tech infrastructure spending.

bullets.title: US hotel RevPAR +12.6% YoY in week ending 10/24 — urban/events-driven, with easy comps ahead
bullets.body: US hotel RevPAR hit $125 (+12.6% YoY; ADR +7.4%, occupancy +4.8%) with luxury at +15.2%. Urban markets led at +16.3%, boosted by event-driven demand: Chicago +40% (PACK Expo), Las Vegas +26% (FABTECH/Money20/20), Tampa +26%. Six of nine remaining 2026 weeks have easy YoY comparisons; 4Q26 is tracking US RevPAR +8.2%.

bullets.title: JPM AM morning note: long AI momentum/semis into MegaCap earnings; risks include FOMC, election regulation, and Middle East escalation
bullets.body: JPM's portfolio solutions desk favors long AI Momentum (ex-'AI Vulnerables') as beta-neutral positioning with risks fading. DRAM +10.2% and Semis +6.9% over three sessions post-Hynix earnings signal strong near-term AI chip demand. Key upcoming risks flagged: hyperscaler capex commentary from AMZN/GOOGL/MSFT/INTC, FOMC, election regulation risk, IPO liquidity drain, and potential Middle East escalation post-election. S&P 500 trades at ~18x 2027.

bullets.title: UK Budget: borrowing rises to £133B (4.2% of GDP) but macro impact limited; JPMorgan more optimistic than OBR on growth
bullets.body: The UK Budget pushed FY26/27 borrowing up £8B (0.2% of GDP) and fiscal headroom narrows to £15B, contingent on future tightening. OBR downgraded 2027 growth to 1.0% from 1.6% but JPMorgan forecasts 1.6%/1.5% for 2026/2027, suggesting actual borrowing will come in below OBR projections. Structural primary deficit expected to fall 0.6% annually through 2030/31 — an ongoing drag on UK growth.

bullets.title: 10yr at 5% with oil at $102: macro regime watch — higher energy + higher rates increasingly concerning
bullets.body: Oppenheimer's industrial/macro desk flags that the historically supportive backdrop (10yr below 5%, oil near $80) has shifted: 10yr at 5.0% combined with WTI at $102 is flagged as 'concerning' vs. the prior supportive regime. Treasury yields are down 30+ bps since Oct 8 on capex sustainability concerns, but the negative correlation between yields and stocks broke in early October — a regime shift to monitor.

bullets.title: ADP raises FY27 EPS guidance to +10-12%; payroll backdrop remains 'low-hire, low-fire'
bullets.body: ADP Q1 revenue $5.49B beat consensus; FY27 EPS guidance raised to +10-12% from +9-11% and revenue guidance raised to ~6%. US pays per control growth is broad-based and consistent with a low-hire, low-fire employment environment. Client funds interest revenue raised $50M to $1.59-1.61B on 3.8% yield. Margin expansion of 70-90bps maintained as productivity gains are reinvested into AI, cloud, and go-to-market.

bullets.title: 52-week lows sweep: NFLX -43.6%, UBER -32.3%, BKNG -29.3%, ENPH -32% YTD — broad-based momentum unwind
bullets.body: StreetAccount flagged 66 stocks hitting 52-week lows vs. 83 at highs in Wednesday's session. Notable YTD decliners include Netflix -43.6%, Uber -32.3%, Booking -29.3%, and Enphase -32%. Finance and Health Technology sectors are the most active on both sides. This breadth dynamic is consistent with the 'high-beta momentum down ~15% over the month' noted by Hedgeye.
